(4) Skip-guard follows the determinism-test mold: module-level pytestmark skipif on _required_data_present() checking data/f1_data_<year>.db for {2022,2023,2024} + params/retro_truth dir; skips cleanly when absent, RUNS here (data present - verified, test ran not skipped). (5) Round-trip uses shape/equality assertions, not tolerances. Test is behavior-focused on the protected guarantee.

r6-test-rerun.title: Re-run integration test + time it
r6-test-rerun.imperative: Re-run py -m pytest tests/integration/test_module_record_emit.py -q myself; expect 1 passed, NOT skipped. Time it and explain the 1.75s anomaly with the true cause. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r6-test-rerun.finding: Re-ran py -m pytest tests/integration/test_module_record_emit.py -q myself: '1 passed in 0.90s' (0.75s call), NOT skipped (data present). TIMING ANOMALY EXPLAINED with the true cause, not hand-waving: I independently instrumented the test's exact train+2-backtest path. Results: TRAIN wall=0.692s, BACKTEST off=0.016s, BACKTEST on=0.018s, TOTAL=0.726s -- matching pytest's call time. The reported 1.75s vs my 0.90s is import/cache-warmth variance; both sub-2s. The speed is REAL training at deliberately microscopic scale, NOT caching/reuse/skip: (1) GOLD_CYCLE_REUSE_EXISTING env var is UNSET (verified None) so the reuse short-circuits in cmd_train/cmd_backtest are inactive; (2) the test uses a fresh tmp_path for both train and backtest, so no prior manifest exists to reuse and there are NO session/module fixtures (only tmp_path); (3) the smoke bundle manifest confirms real training happened with these budgets: epochs_run=2, train_event_count=2 (1 round x 2 yrs), eval_event_count=1, final_train_loss=0.214. With max_rounds_per_year=1 the network trains on 2 tiny events (20 entities), hidden_dim 32, 2 epochs -- sub-second is expected and correct. The test IS self-contained on a clean checkout.

r7-seeding-isolation.title: RNG-seeding isolation logic
r7-seeding-isolation.imperative: Verify the torch.manual_seed isolation logic is sound and honestly documented in the test docstring; confirm the pre-existing training-mode/dropout defect rationale is accurate. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r7-seeding-isolation.finding: Isolation logic is SOUND and HONESTLY documented; I verified the underlying claim against src. (1) load_latent_power_module_bundle (latent_power_bundle.py:88-118) constructs the module and load_state_dict but NEVER calls .eval() -> a fresh nn.Module defaults to train() mode, so the loaded bundle is in training mode. (2) evaluate_labeled_batches (module_training_orchestration.py:581) runs inference under torch.no_grad() with NO .eval() anywhere -> no_grad disables grad but NOT dropout, so dropout is stochastic at inference. Both facts match the test docstring verbatim. Consequently un-seeded sequential backtests draw different dropout masks -> different JSON; pinning torch.manual_seed(0) before EACH call forces both onto the identical RNG path -> identical masks -> byte-identical JSON. This isolates the flag's effect (which must be nil on the payload) from pre-existing dropout nondeterminism; it does NOT mask the flag -- if the flag mutated the payload the seeded runs would still differ. The rationale is documented in 3 places (module docstring, _run_backtest docstring, _TORCH_SEED comment) and names the defect honestly. Independently reproduced byte-equality under this exact seeding (off==on, 1856 bytes). The pre-existing dropout-at-inference defect is correctly attributed and already tracked as tc3 -- not re-litigated here.

r8-byte-equality-raw.title: Raw byte-equality assertion
r8-byte-equality-raw.imperative: Verify byte-equality is asserted RAW (no normalization, no tolerance, no bundle_manifest_path fallback). Confirm sidecar-only-flag-on and load_module_record round-trip assertions are genuine. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r8-byte-equality-raw.finding: Byte-equality is RAW. Test line 208-214: bytes_off=out_off.read_bytes(); bytes_on=out_on.read_bytes(); assert bytes_off==bytes_on. No json.loads-then-compare, no key normalization, no tolerance, and the allowed bundle_manifest_path normalization fallback is NOT present anywhere in the file (grep-confirmed during read). It is genuinely raw bytes because both invocations pass the SAME bundle_path, so the embedded bundle_manifest_path field is already identical (verified in my repro: both outputs 1856 bytes, identical). Sidecar-only-flag-on is genuine: _sidecar_paths derives {stem}.record.npz/.json; asserts NOT npz_off.exists() and NOT json_off.exists() for flag-off, and npz_on.exists()/json_on.exists() for flag-on. load_module_record round-trip is genuine and non-trivial: loads the real flag-on record, reads event_count from the backtest JSON, asserts len(record['events'])==event_count, and per event asserts pi is ndarray of shape (n,), sigma_pi ndarray (n,n), len(entity_ids)==n. I independently reproduced the same round-trip on the smoke record (n=20, pi (20,), sigma (20,20), counts match). Assertions are concrete and load-bearing, not smoke-and-mirrors.

r10-details-noecho.imperative: Open the actual details.json in smoke_reports/ and confirm it lacks emit_module_record (top-level and run_config), not just trust the prose. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r10-details-noecho.finding: Opened the actual details.json on disk (smoke_reports/gold_cycle_260605_234006_2022thru2023_smoke1.details.json), not just the prose. emit_module_record is absent at top level (18 keys, none is the flag), absent in run_config (29 keys, listed - includes output_dir/emit_fusion_train_rows/seed/etc but NOT emit_module_record), and the substring 'emit_module_record' does not appear ANYWHERE in the serialized blob. r11-pollution.title: Pollution check outside evidence dir
r11-pollution.imperative: Verify the smoke run wrote nothing outside the evidence dir; check outputs/evo_runs, reports/evo, params/gold for files with mtime in the run window. Distinguish pre-existing smoke1 files by timestamp/slug. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r11-pollution.finding: POLLUTION CONFIRMED. The smoke run wrote ONE file outside the evidence dir: params/gold/uncertainty_calibration/unc_cal_260605_234006_2022thru2023_smoke1.json. Proof it is THIS run's output (not the pre-existing smoke1 the handoff warned about): its mtime is 2026-06-05 16:41:37 == this run's end (log/summary/details/unc_diag all 16:41:37), and its slug 260605_234006_2022thru2023_smoke1 is byte-identical to this run's report slug (gold_cycle_260605_234006_2022thru2023_smoke1.*). The genuinely pre-existing smoke1 is unc_cal_260520_214442_2023thru2023_smoke1.json (mtime 07:58:53, May-20 slug) -- correctly distinguished and NOT counted. outputs/evo_runs: NO new files (clean). reports/evo: newest files 07:58:55 (pre-existing, clean). Root cause: src/evo_predictor/gold_cycle/runner.py:341-343 hardcodes the calibration path to params/gold/uncertainty_calibration/{slug}.json, ignoring config output_dir/report_dir (every other artifact respects report_dir). So this escape is unavoidable for ANY smoke run without a src change -- which is forbidden in G4. This BREACHES the close criterion 'smoke run wrote nothing outside evidence/' and the config's own comment. The implementer should at minimum have DISCLOSED the escaped file in g4-smoke-run.md and flagged it; instead the evidence is silent. Captured as triage tc1. Not the test-author's bug to patch, but the criterion is objectively unmet and the evidence overclaims.

consolidation.summary: BLOCK on evidence-validity grounds. TEST deliverable is excellent and fully verified (re-run 1 passed not skipped; timing anomaly explained as real micro-scale training not caching/reuse - train 0.69s + backtest 0.016s independently reproduced, GOLD_CYCLE_REUSE_EXISTING unset, fresh tmp_path, epochs_run=2 confirmed; raw byte-equality with NO normalization reproduced at 1856 bytes; seed-pin isolation logic verified sound against src and honestly documented in 3 places; sidecar-only-flag-on and load_module_record round-trip genuine; simplification PASS; ZERO tracked or untracked src/configs/docs diffs). The SMOKE EVIDENCE package fails ONE stated close criterion: the run wrote params/gold/uncertainty_calibration/unc_cal_260605_234006_2022thru2023_smoke1.json OUTSIDE the evidence dir (mtime 16:41:37 == run end; slug identical to this run's reports), breaching the 'writes nothing outside evidence/' contract and the config's own comment, and the evidence markdown does NOT disclose it (overclaims cleanliness by omission). Root cause is a hardcoded src path (runner.py:341-343) the implementer was forbidden to change, so the remedy is NOT a src patch in this gate: (1) remove/relocate the escaped artifact so it cannot be accidentally committed, (2) disclose the escape honestly in g4-smoke-run.md, (3) flag the hardcoded-path defect (captured as triage tc1) for Commander. Narrow, remediable block; all 10 non-pollution checks pass.

triage_candidates.statement: Gold-cycle hardcodes the uncertainty-calibration artifact path to params/gold/uncertainty_calibration/{slug}.json (src/evo_predictor/gold_cycle/runner.py:341-343), ignoring the config's output_dir/report_dir. Consequently ANY bounded/smoke run -- including isolated agent-work runs -- promotes a calibration JSON into the repo's params/gold tree, defeating output isolation. The G4 smoke run did exactly this (unc_cal_260605_234006_2022thru2023_smoke1.json). Recommend an issue to route the calibration artifact through report_dir/output_dir (or a configurable promotion toggle) so smoke/evidence runs stay self-contained. Out of scope for G4 (src change forbidden).
